children: Several leading technology suppliers have significantly increased AI server prices by up to 45% months after contract agreements were made, according to reporting by the Financial Times.
The price hikes have impacted major financial trading firms such as Jane Street, Optiver, and Hudson River Trading as they expand data center operations, sources said.

One person familiar with the situation described the increases as “disconcerting,” citing examples of 25%, 30%, and even 45% price rises between the time of contract agreement and final delivery of components.
"There is a significant disparity between the price initially agreed months in advance and the amount that companies end up paying once the components are delivered," the person added.

The report notes that surging memory costs—up more than 400% since the start of 2024, according to JPMorgan research—are a key driver behind these server price increases. As a result, GPU server prices have risen at least 20-30%, with CPU nodes, where memory makes up a sizable share of the cost, having tripled or more, sources said.
In one publicized dispute, British trading firm XTX sued Dell in Irish court in June following an alleged price hike. According to court documents, XTX and Dell

agreed to a fixed $549M, supplemented by a $5 million payment for price certainty. But Dell later asserted that increased component costs required XTX to pay an additional $62-70M to receive the servers. XTX claimed surprise at Dell’s move, alleging that Dell referenced other companies that had ultimately accepted price adjustments after exploring alternatives. XTX said Dell indicated it "was not able to absorb those increased costs" attributable to rising memory prices.
The Financial Times reports that HP Enterprise
declined to comment on the price adjustments, while Dell and Lenovo
did not respond to multiple requests. Similarly, Hudson River Trading and Optiver declined to comment, and Jane Street did not respond.

title: Tech suppliers jack up AI server prices after contracts inked - FT
